To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Vibrio cholera O1 produces an extracellular matrix when exposed to antibody mediated agluttination and that ECM production is associated with complement resistance.
Vibrio cholera is able to produce an extracellular polysaccharide matrix (ECM), or capsule, when agglutinated or immobilized by antibodies.

Vibrio cholera, upon encountering intestinal antibodies, secretes an extracelluar matrix (ECM), or O antigen capsule, which may protect it from additional host immune defenses and enable it to exit a hostile environment.

the role of the extracellular matrix in the pathogenesis of Vibrio cholera.
how the bacterium V. cholera secretes an extracelluar matrix (ECM, or capsule) in response to antibody agglutination in the intestinal lumi.
the interaction of the cholera toxin producing bacterium Vibrio cholera O1 with antibodies produced by the immune system of the human host.
